summary: The closeout report is accurate and well scoped on its main points. It says plainly that the weak-scaling performance objective was not met (4-node efficiency 53-55%), and it keeps that separate from execution and correctness success. All three stages are reported separately with the correct baselines. Every headline number I checked matches the retained evidence: Stage 1 medians, historical deltas, CV and drift; Stage 2 paired time changes against validation.json; Stage 3 medians, R(N)/(N*R(1)) efficiencies, loop durations, CV, drift, per-node event ranges, and job elapsed times and exit codes in scheduler.txt. verify_archive.py recomputes medians from runs.csv, recomputes paired ratios from same-node loop times separately from the median rates, and replays Stage 3 rank placement. The build, input, timing, GDS and cache limits are disclosed. The archive is compact: no XTC data, builds, pixel or timestamp arrays, or transcripts. Its roughly 9 MB of retained scripts, tests and receipts are worth keeping. One blocking problem remains. NEXT_STEPS.md cites an 'existing network inspection' through a hardware.md anchor that does not exist in this checkout, so its claim about a narrower configured Lustre path has no support. One non-blocking bookkeeping item: review.md and the manifest's results_review are still placeholders and must be updated with this review before the push.
checks: Stage 3 efficiencies in README.md:41-44 recomputed by hand from the medians: S 2334.3/(2*1685.8)=69.2%, 3586.6/(4*1685.8)=53.2%; E 68.6%/53.2%; EC 71.1%/55.0%; ECC 71.3%/55.0%. All match summary.json weak_efficiency_percent.

Stage 1 table in README.md:15-18 matches stage1-original-results.json: medians, change_percent (+1.74/+0.72/+1.34/+1.59 and +0.57/+0.95/+0.85/+0.05), max CV 2.653%, max abs S drift 2.667%. The report discloses that this snapshot's pending status is historical.

Stage 2 paired time changes in README.md:28-31 match validation.json paired_time_change_percent after rounding (0.53, -0.27, -0.07, 0.28, 0.92, 0.21, 0.72, 0.02). CV 3.77% and drift 1.36% match stage2-prior-review.json.

Stage 3 n04 summary.json: time CV values of 0.49/0.31/0.52/0.19% are all below 0.7%; the largest drift deviation is 1-0.98494=1.51%. Loop durations implied by the medians are 59.3-63.8 s, 85.7-89.5 s and 110.6-116.3 s, consistent with README.md:46.
bd-placement-verification.json gives a 2-node per-node event range of 97.8k-102.2k, matching README.md:48.
scheduler.txt: all 12 measurement jobs are COMPLETED 0:0, and their elapsed times match the job table in README.md:52-54.

verify_archive.py checks: 159/108 case counts; events and rates against loop_seconds; requested_bytes = events*3358200; rank completeness and absence of errors; Stage 3 host, physical-core and GPU-PCI uniqueness; medians; weak efficiency; same-node P/C paired ratios computed from loop times; bundle map hashes, syntax and bundle.json consistency; device receipts.

cases.jsonl sample (stage3-weak-n04/r3-anchor-S): compact per-rank records with host, device, affinity and memory data. No pixel or timestamp arrays; loop_diagnostic is explicitly labeled diagnostic_only.

The NEXT_STEPS arithmetic checks out: 2.4M events * 3,358,200 B = 8.06 TB; 24 nodes * 4 * 200 Gb/s = 2.4 TB/s; 12.916 GiB/s (cpp-read stripe-screen count 2, 40 threads) * 24 nodes * 60 s = about 20 TB.
catalog.json and docs/performance/README.md add only the new campaign entry and a summary that matches the report.

manifest.json lists the scope, a status of complete, performance_outcome unsuccessful_scaleout, all 12 jobs and the raw locations. review.md is not hashed in the manifest, so updating it does not change any recorded hash.
Archive and scripts READMEs explicitly exclude datasets, builds, caches, full raw output and transcripts, and state the limits of the CPU tests' portability and of relaunching.
limitations: Read-only review: I ran no verifier, tests, sacct, hash checks or git commands. Those results are the coordinator's, plus the retained validation.json.
I could not read raw scratch outputs under /pscratch. Raw-hash ledger agreement and the bundle restorations come from the coordinator's statement.
I could not browse, so I did not verify the external NERSC, CUG and OpenSFS figures in NEXT_STEPS.md (7.8 TB/s, 40.8 GB/s, 4,003,761 MB/s, slide and section references).
I spot-checked runs.csv, cases.jsonl and the manifest rather than reading every row and line. Full-coverage arithmetic relies on verify_archive.py logic, which I inspected but did not execute.
I did not inspect every frozen bundle file or the Stage 3 support tests line by line. I reviewed retention against scope and the README claims.

findings.evidence: The link '../../../../hardware.md#perlmutter-network-and-lustre-capacity--november-23-2026' resolves to psana/psana/gpu/docs/performance/hardware.md. That file's only headings are 'Hardware and cache semantics', 'Ampere node inventory — October 26, 2026', 'Hardware used by the recent campaigns' and 'What cold and warm mean'. Searching psana/psana/gpu for 'Perlmutter network and Lustre capacity' finds nothing. The claim that 'the existing network inspection observed a narrower configured Lustre path on one node' therefore has no retained source in this checkout.
findings.requested_change: Point the link at a committed artifact that actually records the one-node NIC/LNet inspection, giving its path and job. If no such artifact is in scope, remove the sentence or label it as unarchived, and keep only the instruction to verify the client/LNet configuration.

findings.evidence: review.md says 'Independent report/archive review pending', and manifest.json has review.independent_results 'pending closeout review' and lifecycle.results_review 'pending'. Meanwhile README.md:72 says the review record 'covers this final report and archive'.
findings.requested_change: Before pushing, record the final reviewed SHA, verdict and findings and their resolution in review.md, and update the manifest's review and lifecycle fields to match. If the manifest changes, regenerate its hashes and rerun check_catalog.py and verify_archive.py.
